bestBets.overview: Handy maiden. LA REINA VEGA is the pick because she's fit and she's proven on a Seymour heavy 9. That was her debut run which was a solid performance in a good form race. She had her chance last time at long odds on but it was still a sound effort. AUTUMN IN GRINZING starts her 2nd prep. She was luckless and sound here 14 weeks ago. She has jumped out well.  KEEN OBSERVER stretches out to 1400m with two solid efforts under his belt.

raceTips.comment:
Keen Observer ran well as favourite in a strong race last start at Geelong. He looks the potential leader, handles wet ground and has Blake Shinn in the saddle. 
La Reina Vega was an eye-catcher on heavy ground on debut before she was narrowly beaten as an odds-on fav on the synthetic last start. No surprise to see her win back on turf. 
Clementaro ran the second-fastest last 200m of the race/meeting on debut. The rise in distance looks ideal and he seems well over the odds in early betting at $51+.

bestBets.overview: There were two huge runs against the pattern of the day at Moe, August 13. One was Snitchy who went to Wang. and won on Sunday. The other was JONQUIL in the 2050m maiden. From a wide draw she settled down a mile away. The effort was outstanding to get as close as she did. That's two starts now in this distance range for her two best performances. The heavy box was well and truly ticked last time. ROCK CATCHER is a chance but the D Lane tax is in play as $2.30 chance in early markets. She finished 2L ahead of 26 start maiden BOLSHIE and on the run to the line in that race wasn't all that inferior.  He's a 20/1 chance here. Of course conceding that ROCK CATCHER has the upside. BOLSHIE has had one start in this distance range for one of his better efforts.  FIERCE FIASCO tries 2000m for the first time. He's going well. KNUCKLEHEAD wouldn't shock.

raceTips.comment:
Jonquil's run was potentially massive in hindsight last start given the subsequent results and track bias on the day. She came from a mile back on the turn on a day being on speed and on the rail was a massive advantage. She was unlucky not to win her only other 2000m start. 
Rock Catcher started $3.80 at her Australian debut last start and was doing her best work late. The rise in distance is a positive and Damian Lane sticking with her is another big tick. She still has to tick the heavy track box and you have to take short odds. 
Baldoni looks the blowout at huge odds. He ran the fastest last 200m of the race last start at Bairnsdale. With the rise in distance, the inside barrier and blinkers going on for the first time, he could settle much closer and could improve sharply.
